AGENTS.md:1:# AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md:2:
AGENTS.md:3:BUVIS gems monorepo. Python toolkit (buvis-pybase + zettel) and CLI tools, shipped as a single PyPI package `buvis-gems`. Supports Python 3.11+.
AGENTS.md:4:
AGENTS.md:5:## Reading these instructions
AGENTS.md:6:
AGENTS.md:7:This root `AGENTS.md` is the always-on canonical guidance. Some directories also
AGENTS.md:8:carry their own nested `AGENTS.md` with rules scoped to the code beside them.
AGENTS.md:9:Before working on files in a directory, discover and read any `AGENTS.md` on the
AGENTS.md:10:path from the repo root down to that directory, and follow it for files in its
AGENTS.md:11:scope. Do this yourself even if your host did not load those files automatically
AGENTS.md:12:— host loading of nested files varies and is not guaranteed (see
AGENTS.md:13:[`docs/dev/architecture/agent-host-support.md`](docs/dev/architecture/agent-host-support.md)).
AGENTS.md:14:
AGENTS.md:15:## Quick Start
AGENTS.md:16:
AGENTS.md:17:```bash
AGENTS.md:18:uv sync --all-groups --all-extras            # install deps
AGENTS.md:19:pre-commit install                          # setup hooks
AGENTS.md:20:uv run pytest                               # run tests
AGENTS.md:21:uv run pytest -m snapshot                   # run snapshot tests only (skipped off canonical env)
AGENTS.md:22:uv run pytest --snapshot-update             # regenerate snapshot baselines (local use only)
AGENTS.md:23:uv run mypy src/lib/ src/tools/              # type check
AGENTS.md:24:uv run sphinx-build -b html docs/source docs/build/html  # build docs
AGENTS.md:25:```
AGENTS.md:26:
AGENTS.md:27:## Architecture
AGENTS.md:28:
AGENTS.md:29:```text
AGENTS.md:30:src/
AGENTS.md:31:├── lib/buvis/pybase/           # shared library (namespace pkg: no buvis/__init__.py)
AGENTS.md:32:│   ├── adapters/               # jira, console, config adapters
AGENTS.md:33:│   ├── configuration/          # settings/config helpers
AGENTS.md:34:│   ├── filesystem/             # file utilities
AGENTS.md:35:│   ├── formatting/             # output formatting
AGENTS.md:36:│   └── zettel/                 # zettel subsystem
AGENTS.md:37:│       ├── domain/             # entities, services, interfaces, value objects
AGENTS.md:38:│       ├── application/        # use cases
AGENTS.md:39:│       ├── infrastructure/     # formatters, repositories, file parsers
AGENTS.md:40:│       └── integrations/       # jira assemblers
AGENTS.md:41:└── tools/
AGENTS.md:42:    ├── bim/                    # BUVIS InfoMesh CLI (zettel integration)
AGENTS.md:43:    ├── dot/                    # dotfiles manager
AGENTS.md:44:    ├── fctracker/              # foreign currency tracker
AGENTS.md:45:    ├── fren/                   # file renamer toolkit
AGENTS.md:46:    ├── morph/                  # file conversion toolkit
AGENTS.md:47:    ├── muc/                    # music collection tools
AGENTS.md:48:    ├── netscan/                # network scanning tools
AGENTS.md:49:    ├── outlookctl/             # Outlook CLI
AGENTS.md:50:    ├── pinger/                 # ICMP ping utilities
AGENTS.md:51:    ├── puc/                    # photo utility collection
AGENTS.md:52:    ├── readerctl/              # Readwise Reader CLI
AGENTS.md:53:    ├── sysup/                  # system update tools
AGENTS.md:54:    ├── vuc/                    # video utility collection
AGENTS.md:55:    └── zseq/                   # Zettelsequence utilities
AGENTS.md:56:tests/
AGENTS.md:57:├── lib/                        # library tests
AGENTS.md:58:│   ├── pybase/
AGENTS.md:59:│   ├── zettel/
AGENTS.md:60:│   └── zettel_integrations/
AGENTS.md:61:└── tools/                      # CLI tool tests
AGENTS.md:62:tools/                          # Dev command shims (on PATH via mise) + helpers
AGENTS.md:63:├── release                     # public shim → mise `release` task
AGENTS.md:64:└── lib/                        # helpers, invoked by path (NOT on PATH)
AGENTS.md:65:    ├── release                 # release impl: bump+tag+push
AGENTS.md:66:    ├── pin_deps.py             # pin deps from uv.lock for publishing
AGENTS.md:67:    ├── scaffold.py             # scaffold a new tool
AGENTS.md:68:    ├── check_audit_ignores.py  # pip-audit suppression guard (+ audit/ config)
AGENTS.md:69:    ├── check_tool_wiring.py    # pre-commit tool-wiring check
AGENTS.md:70:    ├── parity_brief_portfolio.py
AGENTS.md:71:    └── gen_zettel_writer_fixtures.py
AGENTS.md:72:```
AGENTS.md:73:
AGENTS.md:74:**Key patterns:**
AGENTS.md:75:
AGENTS.md:76:- **Single package**: `buvis-gems` on PyPI, one `uv tool install`
AGENTS.md:77:- **Namespace package**: `src/lib/buvis/` has no `__init__.py`
AGENTS.md:78:- **Hatch packages**: each `src/tools/<name>/` maps to top-level `<name>` in wheel
AGENTS.md:79:- **Libraries are internal**: pybase + zettel not published separately
AGENTS.md:80:- **All-interface rule**: every command/action must work across CLI, TUI, API, and WebUI
AGENTS.md:81:
AGENTS.md:82:## Tool Structure
AGENTS.md:83:
AGENTS.md:84:Every tool under `src/tools/<name>/` follows a base layout:
AGENTS.md:85:
AGENTS.md:86:```text
AGENTS.md:87:tool_name/
AGENTS.md:88:├── __init__.py
AGENTS.md:89:├── __main__.py
AGENTS.md:90:├── cli.py              # Click entry point
AGENTS.md:91:├── settings.py         # Tool-specific settings
AGENTS.md:92:└── commands/           # One module per CLI command
AGENTS.md:93:```
AGENTS.md:94:
AGENTS.md:95:Add subdirs only when needed:
AGENTS.md:96:
AGENTS.md:97:| Dir | When | Example |
AGENTS.md:98:|-----|------|---------|
AGENTS.md:99:| `adapters/` | External service clients | fctracker, readerctl |
AGENTS.md:100:| `domain/` | Business logic beyond simple commands | fctracker |
AGENTS.md:101:| `shared/` | Code reused across commands | zseq |
AGENTS.md:102:
AGENTS.md:103:> `bim/commands/serve/frontend/` contains the WebUI SvelteKit app — the only tool with a frontend subtree.
AGENTS.md:104:
AGENTS.md:105:> `bim/commands/doc/` follows the existing `commands/serve/`-style group pattern with a `shared/` subdir holding cross-command utilities (pipeline, OCR/classifier/extractor adapters, state DB, issuer registry, zettel writer).
AGENTS.md:106:
AGENTS.md:107:## Code Conventions
AGENTS.md:108:
AGENTS.md:109:**Type hints** — modern style, no `Optional`:
AGENTS.md:110:
AGENTS.md:111:```python
AGENTS.md:112:from __future__ import annotations
AGENTS.md:113:def foo(path: Path | None = None) -> list[str]: ...
AGENTS.md:114:```
AGENTS.md:115:
AGENTS.md:116:**Imports**:
AGENTS.md:117:
AGENTS.md:118:- Explicit `__all__` in `__init__.py`
AGENTS.md:119:- `TYPE_CHECKING` guards for type-only imports
AGENTS.md:120:
AGENTS.md:121:**Docstrings**: Google format
AGENTS.md:122:
AGENTS.md:123:**CLI pattern**: Click-based. `buvis_options` adds `--version`, `--config`, `--log-level`, `--debug`, and `--update` to every tool automatically:
AGENTS.md:124:
AGENTS.md:125:```python
AGENTS.md:126:@click.command()
AGENTS.md:127:@buvis_options
AGENTS.md:128:@click.pass_context
AGENTS.md:129:def cli(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
AGENTS.md:130:    settings = get_settings(ctx)
AGENTS.md:131:    ...
AGENTS.md:132:```
AGENTS.md:133:
AGENTS.md:134:**Lazy imports in CLI handlers**: import command classes inside handler functions, not at module level. This avoids pulling in optional/heavy dependencies before the user picks a subcommand:
AGENTS.md:135:
AGENTS.md:136:```python
AGENTS.md:137:@cli.command("create")
AGENTS.md:138:@click.pass_context
AGENTS.md:139:def create(ctx):
AGENTS.md:140:    from bim.commands.create_note.create_note import CommandCreateNote
AGENTS.md:141:    ...
AGENTS.md:142:```
AGENTS.md:143:
AGENTS.md:144:## Error Handling
AGENTS.md:145:
AGENTS.md:146:**Command layer** (`commands/`):
AGENTS.md:147:- Return `CommandResult` for all outcomes — success and failure
AGENTS.md:148:- Catch expected exceptions (e.g. `FileNotFoundError`) internally, return `CommandResult(success=False, error=str(exc))`
AGENTS.md:149:- No `console.panic()` or `sys.exit()` inside command classes
AGENTS.md:150:- No custom exception classes for control flow
AGENTS.md:151:
AGENTS.md:152:**CLI layer** (`cli.py`):
AGENTS.md:153:- Inspect `CommandResult` and call `console.panic()` / `console.failure()` / `console.success()`
AGENTS.md:154:- Use `console.report_result()` for standardized output
AGENTS.md:155:- Catch `ImportError` for optional deps, call `console.require_import()`
AGENTS.md:156:- Catch `FatalError` for unrecoverable infrastructure failures
AGENTS.md:157:
AGENTS.md:158:**Click argument validation**:
AGENTS.md:159:- Avoid parse-time validators that short-circuit before the callback (`click.Path(exists=True)`, `IntRange`, custom `ParamType.convert` that raises). They emit Click's default `Usage: ... Error: ...` formatting and bypass the buvis console.
AGENTS.md:160:- Validate inside the callback instead: `if not path.is_file(): console.panic(f"file not found: {path}"); return`.
AGENTS.md:161:- `click.Choice` is the exception — its parse-time error lists the valid values, which is more useful than a rewritten message.
AGENTS.md:162:
AGENTS.md:163:**Console methods**:
AGENTS.md:164:- Fatal (exit): `console.panic(msg)` — prints + exits with code 1
AGENTS.md:165:- Recoverable: `console.failure(msg)` — prints, continues
AGENTS.md:166:- Status: `console.success()`, `console.warning()`, `console.info()`
AGENTS.md:167:- All user-facing output must route through `console`. No `print()`, `sys.stdout.write()`, `sys.stderr.write()`, `click.echo()`, `click.secho()`, or the Python logging module. Plain writes bypass the buvis prefix markers (`✘`, `✓`, etc.) and become indistinguishable from stray output, which is what makes a missed `console.panic` look like a print statement to the user.
AGENTS.md:168:- The one sanctioned exception is the `dot filter` clean/smudge plumbing, which writes git's blob payload as raw bytes on stdout and at most one error line on stderr, because git owns both streams and a console marker would corrupt the payload (discovery R12).
AGENTS.md:169:- Never let raw exceptions (stack traces) reach the user.
AGENTS.md:170:
AGENTS.md:171:## Invariants (evolution guardrails)
AGENTS.md:172:
AGENTS.md:173:These encode the failure classes surfaced by the 2026-07-09 evolution assessment (`docs/dev/project-management/reviews/evolution-assessment-2026-07-09.md`). Each is either **HOLDS** (enforce it) or a **GAP** (a tracked PRD is closing it — write new code to the target state, not the current one).
AGENTS.md:174:
AGENTS.md:175:- **Atomic persistence** — never persist a note, state file, or config with a bare `Path.write_text`/`open(...,"w")`. Use `pybase.filesystem.atomic_write` (tempfile + fsync + `os.replace`). Truncate-then-write loses data on crash/ENOSPC. *HOLDS for the library and note/updater write paths (00041) — keep it, except `ConfigWriter.write` (`configuration/config_writer.py`), which still does a bare `write_text` — deliberately out of scope for 00041. GAP → pidash was closed by retiring pidash (00071); autopilot-state durability now lives in the buvis home repo (tracon/statectl), not gems.*
AGENTS.md:176:- **Confine request-derived paths** — any filesystem path built from an HTTP request / external input must be `resolve()`d and asserted under an allowed root before read/write/delete/open. Network-facing servers must have auth + `TrustedHostMiddleware`. *HOLDS (00042) — bim serve confines request paths via `confine_path` (403 outside the vault/archive roots), mints a startup token required as `X-Buvis-Token`, installs `TrustedHostMiddleware`, and warns on a non-loopback bind (`commands/serve/_security.py`). Keep it.*
AGENTS.md:177:- **The library stays interface-agnostic** — `src/lib/buvis/pybase/` must not import a UI framework at module import time or emit output outside the console adapter. No import-time Click monkey-patching, no `sys.exit`/`click.echo`/`print` in lib code. A TUI/API/WebUI process must be able to `import` settings without pulling Click. *HOLDS (00052) — keep it.*
AGENTS.md:178:- **One action, one implementation across interfaces** — CLI/TUI/API/WebUI adapters must drive the same command class / use case through the composition root and return `CommandResult`; do not reimplement business logic per interface (dot's TUI is the anti-pattern; bim's serve action registry is the exemplar). *HOLDS (00051 design → 00053/00054) — the all-interface seam design (00051) is realized: dot's git ops unified behind `DotGitService` (00053) and bim's serve/TUI converged on the shared action registry (00054). Keep it.*
AGENTS.md:179:- **Claim/lifecycle release on any exit** — resource claims and locks release in `finally` (or catch `BaseException`), never only `except Exception`; `KeyboardInterrupt` must not leak a claim. *HOLDS (00044) — the bim doc claim/dedup pipeline releases claims and locks in `finally` (`commands/doc/shared/`); keep it.*
AGENTS.md:180:- **`CommandResult` discipline** — commands return `CommandResult`; the CLI/adapter layer renders it (`console.report_result`) and maps exit/HTTP status. No `sys.exit`/`console.panic` inside command classes. *HOLDS in `src/tools/*/commands/**` — keep it.*
AGENTS.md:181:- **Clean-architecture layering + tool isolation** — zettel `domain → application → infrastructure → integrations` one-directional; no cross-tool imports; no `src/lib → src/tools`. *HOLDS — keep it.*
AGENTS.md:182:
AGENTS.md:183:## Testing
AGENTS.md:184:
AGENTS.md:185:- pytest + pytest-mock + pytest-cov
AGENTS.md:186:- Tests in `tests/` mirror `src/lib/` and `src/tools/` structure
AGENTS.md:187:- Mock subprocess calls heavily
AGENTS.md:188:- Class-based test organization
AGENTS.md:189:- **No unused imports/variables**
AGENTS.md:190:- **Markers**: `pytest -m <tool>` runs one tool, `pytest -m lib` runs library tests, `pytest -m "not bim"` excludes a tool. Auto-applied by path in `tests/conftest.py` — no decorators needed. Scaffold registers markers for new tools.
AGENTS.md:191:- **Snapshot tests** (`@pytest.mark.snapshot`) only run on the canonical env (Linux + Python 3.12) — SVG output from Rich/Textual differs across OS/Python so baselines must come from one place. Anywhere else they are auto-skipped. To regenerate baselines run the `update-snapshots` GitHub workflow (`gh workflow run update-snapshots.yml`); it runs `pytest --snapshot-update` on the canonical env and commits the result. Force locally with `BUVIS_SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL=1` only if you know what you're doing.

AGENTS.md:205:## Release
AGENTS.md:206:
AGENTS.md:207:> Full procedure (version authority, checks, destinations, partial-failure recovery): `docs/dev/procedures/releasing.md`.

AGENTS.md:209:```bash

AGENTS.md:211:release --pre rc1                      # pre-release current version to TestPyPI
AGENTS.md:212:release --pre rc1 minor                # bump + pre-release to TestPyPI

AGENTS.md:220:**First-time setup** (already done for buvis-gems):

269:def _reject_out_inside_source(label: str, source: Path, out: Path, items: object = None) -> StepResult | None:
270:    """Reject an ``out`` path that would be re-archived by the run.
271:
272:    An ``out`` under ``source`` makes each run re-archive the previous run's
273:    archive (unbounded recursive growth). ``out`` may not exist yet, so its
274:    PARENT is resolved (which does exist — a stamp only expands the basename) and
275:    the name rejoined, giving a real absolute path to test for containment
276:    against the resolved source. A whole-tree run rejects ``out`` anywhere in
277:    ``source``; a bundle rejects ``out`` equal to the source or equal to or
278:    inside a selected item (invalid ``items`` fail first). Returns a failed
279:    :class:`StepResult` (the caller yields it and returns before walking),
280:    otherwise ``None``.
281:    """
282:    selected: list[Path] = []
283:    if items is not None:
284:        try:
285:            selected = _normalize_items(source, items)
286:        except ValueError as exc:
287:            return StepResult(label, success=False, message=str(exc))
288:    source_resolved = source.resolve()
289:    out_resolved = out.parent.resolve() / out.name
290:    if out_resolved == source_resolved or (items is None and source_resolved in out_resolved.parents):
291:        return StepResult(
292:            label,
293:            success=False,
294:            message=(f"out path {out} is inside source {source}; choose an out path outside the backup source"),
295:        )
296:    for relative in selected:
297:        item = source_resolved / relative
298:        if out_resolved == item or item in out_resolved.parents:

300:                label,
301:                success=False,
302:                message=(

304:                    "choose an out path outside the bundle's items"

388:    """Select bundle members using source-relative excludes and ancestor rules."""
389:    files: list[Path] = []
390:    missing: list[str] = []
391:    total_bytes = file_count = 0
392:    states: dict[str, ExcludeState] = {str(source): state_for_directory(source, base_state)}
393:    applied: list[str] = []
394:    for relative in selected:
395:        path = source / relative
396:        if not _item_present(path):
397:            missing.append(relative.as_posix())
398:            continue
399:        metadata = path.lstat()
400:        state = states[str(source)]
401:        for index, component in enumerate(relative.parts):
402:            ancestor = source.joinpath(*relative.parts[: index + 1])
403:            relpath = ancestor.relative_to(source).as_posix()
404:            if state.is_excluded(component, relpath):
405:                break
406:            if index < len(relative.parts) - 1:
407:                state = state_for_directory(ancestor, state)
408:                states[str(ancestor)] = state
409:                continue
410:            if stat.S_ISDIR(metadata.st_mode):
411:                subtree = _walk_tree(path, state, root=source)
412:                files.extend(subtree.files)
413:                file_count += subtree.file_count
414:                total_bytes += subtree.total_bytes

416:            elif component != BKPIGNORE_FILENAME:

427:def _walk_tree(source: Path, base_state: ExcludeState, *, root: Path | None = None) -> WalkResult:
428:    """Walk ``source`` top-down, applying global excludes + path-scoped ``.bkpignore``.
429:
430:    The exclude state at each directory is the ancestors' state layered with
431:    that directory's own ``.bkpignore`` (if any). Excluded directories are
432:    pruned from further descent; surviving regular files are collected.
433:    """
434:    files: list[Path] = []
435:    symlinks: list[Path] = []
436:    dirs: list[Path] = []
437:    total_bytes = 0
438:    if root is None:
439:        root = source
440:    states: dict[str, ExcludeState] = {str(source): state_for_directory(source, base_state)}
441:
442:    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(source, onerror=_raise_walk_error):
443:        state = states[dirpath]
444:
445:        # Record this surviving directory (the source root, then every descended
446:        # kept subdir) so it is archived non-recursively — otherwise an empty
447:        # directory, and an empty source tree's own `src/` entry, would vanish on
448:        # restore, unlike the former `tar -C ... source`.
449:        dirs.append(Path(dirpath))
450:
451:        kept_dirs: list[str] = []
452:        for dirname in dirnames:
453:            child = os.path.join(dirpath, dirname)
454:            relpath = os.path.relpath(child, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
455:            if state.is_excluded(dirname, relpath):
456:                continue
457:            # A directory symlink: os.walk (followlinks=False) will not descend
458:            # it, and we must NOT read <link>/.bkpignore (it may point outside
459:            # the source tree) — so it stays out of kept_dirs. But the link
460:            # ITSELF is archived as a non-recursive symlink member, so restoring
461:            # preserves it (the former tar backup kept symlinks). tarfile /
462:            # system tar store a symlink as a link without following it.
463:            if os.path.islink(child):
464:                symlinks.append(Path(child))
465:                continue
466:            states[child] = state_for_directory(Path(child), state)
467:            kept_dirs.append(dirname)
468:        dirnames[:] = kept_dirs
469:
470:        for filename in filenames:
471:            if filename == BKPIGNORE_FILENAME:
472:                continue
473:            file_path = Path(dirpath) / filename
474:            relpath = os.path.relpath(file_path, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
475:            if state.is_excluded(filename, relpath):
476:                continue
477:            # Archive a symlink as the link itself (not its target), matching the
478:            # former tar backup — but never stat() it (that follows the link and
479:            # a broken link would raise); a link contributes 0 input bytes.
480:            if file_path.is_symlink():
481:                symlinks.append(file_path)
482:                continue
483:            if not file_path.is_file():
484:                continue
485:            files.append(file_path)
486:            # No suppression: a file we selected but cannot stat is a real error
487:            # for an archiver, not a 0-byte undercount. The runner turns the
488:            # propagated OSError into a failed step.
489:            total_bytes += file_path.stat().st_size
490:
491:    return WalkResult(
492:        files=[*dirs, *files, *symlinks],
493:        total_bytes=total_bytes,
494:        applied=_collect_applied(states),
495:        file_count=len(files),
496:    )

def _emit_progress(progress: Callable[[ProgressEvent], None] | None, event: ProgressEvent) -> None:
    if progress is not None:

def _start_archive_progress(
    label: str, total: int, engine: str, progress: Callable[[ProgressEvent], None] | None
) -> tuple[Callable[[int], None] | None, Callable[[], None]]:
    done = 0 if engine == _ENGINE_PYTHON else None
    reported = done
    emitted_at = time.monotonic()
    _emit_progress(progress, ProgressEvent(label, "archiving", done, total))

    def on_bytes(count: int) -> None:
        nonlocal done, reported, emitted_at
        done = count
        now = time.monotonic()
        if now - emitted_at >= 0.2:
            _emit_progress(progress, ProgressEvent(label, "archiving", done, total))
            reported, emitted_at = done, now

    def on_finalize() -> None:
        if done != reported:
            _emit_progress(progress, ProgressEvent(label, "archiving", done, total))
        _emit_progress(progress, ProgressEvent(label, "finalizing", done, total))

    return (on_bytes if engine == _ENGINE_PYTHON and progress is not None else None), on_finalize

    including empty dirs), then regular files, then symlinks (each archived as
    the link itself, not followed, matching the former tar backup). ``file_count``

    their input sizes (a symlink/dir contributes 0). ``applied`` lists the

        self: WalkResult,
        files: list[Path],
        total_bytes: int,
        applied: list[str],
        file_count: int,

        if engine not in (_ENGINE_PYTHON, _ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR):

            reason = f"unknown engine '{engine}'; expected {_ENGINE_PYTHON} or {_ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR}"

Selected items
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Omit ``items`` to archive the whole source tree, with member names prefixed by
the source directory's name. Set ``items`` to bundle selected files and
directories, with member names relative to ``source``:

.. code-block:: yaml

    instances:
      settings:
        use: tar-archive
        with:
          source: "~"                   # quoted: a bare ~ is YAML null
          out: /Volumes/Backup/settings.tar.gz
          items: [.gitconfig, .config/tool]

Items are literal relative paths, without glob expansion. Redundant separators
and ``.`` components are normalized; duplicate items and children of a selected
directory are included only once. Empty lists, empty paths, absolute paths,
paths normalizing to ``.``, and paths whose first component is ``..`` are
errors; a literal name such as ``..hidden`` is valid. ``items`` must be a list
of strings, and ``items: null`` means the key is omitted (whole tree).
An item cannot pass through a symlink directory. A final symlink, including a
broken one, is archived as a link without following its target.

Excludes still match source-relative paths or basenames. Ancestor and selected
directory ``.bkpignore`` files apply with the same pruning and precedence as a
whole-tree backup. Missing items are listed in the result while present items
are archived. An item that cannot be inspected (for example under an
unreadable directory), an unreadable selected file, or one that disappears
after its presence check fails the step instead of counting as missing.

With ``items``, ``out`` may sit inside ``source`` as long as it is outside every
selected item (for example ``~/.local/backup/settings.tar.gz`` for items
``.gitconfig`` and ``.config/tool``). An ``out`` equal to or inside a selected
item fails in plan, run, and dry-run before anything is written, because the
archive would re-archive itself. An ``out`` equal to ``source`` still fails. A
whole-tree backup (``items`` omitted or ``null``) still rejects any ``out``
inside ``source``. Invalid ``items`` are reported before this check. ``out`` is
judged by its real location, after resolving symlinks in its parent
directory.

The global ``excludes`` list layers via the 00080 ``excludes+`` / ``excludes-``
directives, so a lower layer extends or trims the shared list without re-listing
it:

.. code-block:: yaml

    # buvis-backup.local.yaml  (machine-local, never `dot add`ed)
    excludes+: [scratch-notes]   # add to the inherited list

## [0.17.0] - 2026-11-04

### Added

- **sysup**: on macOS, `rustup update` runs before `mise upgrade` when `rustup` is installed, so the Rust toolchain stays current and mise's `cargo:` tools build with it.
- **gems**: wheels for Python 3.15 (macOS arm64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64), so installing on 3.15 no longer needs a Rust toolchain; `pyyaml` and `xattr` publish no 3.15 wheels yet, so pip and uv build them from source on 3.15 (a C compiler is needed for `xattr`).
- **backup**: TTY runs show per-instance live progress and elapsed time, with input-byte percentages capped at 99% for Python archives and activity only for system tar; `--quiet` hides live status while preserving final results and summary counts.
- **backup**: `--jobs` controls concurrent archive instances (default three); cancellation stops new work, joins workers, stops tar and cleans temporary files while preserving completed results and backups; interruption exits with status 130.
- **backup**: `--plan` previews metadata-only run/skip/fail decisions, reasons and existing-output replacement markers; selected outputs share one timestamp and colliding paths are rejected before plan, run or dry-run execution. Missing inputs report the same errors as a run; a metadata error fails only its instance, keeping its expanded source, while preserving collision checks.
- **backup**: optional `items` bundle literal source-relative files and directories into one archive, preserving empty directories and symlinks while applying inherited exclusions and `.bkpignore` rules.
- **backup**: per-instance `inherit_excludes`, `exclude_remove` and `exclude_add` control inherited exclusions for archives and `--show-excludes`, which still lists the resolved patterns sorted.

### Changed

- **backup**: missing sources and bundles with no surviving members now warn and skip without touching previous archives; each run reports archived or previewed, skipped, and failed step counts. Existing non-directory sources, unreadable sources and unreadable selected items still fail instead of counting as missing; a skipped bundle names its source.

### Fixed

- **backup**: a bundle's `out` may now lie under `source` when it is outside every selected item (for example `~/.local/backup/settings.tar.gz` for `items: [.gitconfig, .npmrc]`); an `out` equal to or inside a selected item still fails in run, `--dry-run` and `--plan`.
- **backup**: progress returns to archiving when a failure after system tar finishes triggers the Python fallback.
- **backup**: interruption during submission or result collection preserves every instance's outcome and finishes cleanup without waiting for a lost completion notification.
- **sysup**: a `timeout` on a captured multi-command shell step now stops the whole step; before, only bash died and the command it was waiting on kept running. Such a step runs in its own process group, so Ctrl-C is forwarded to it, a terminal prompt it raises stops it until the timeout, and a command it runs as root through `sudo` is still out of reach and survives. Interactive steps and steps without a timeout are unchanged
